The DRM level streaming apps (Netflix, Prime Video, Disney+) read to pick HD or SD. Like the attestation, root hiding cannot change it.
This device has no Widevine plugin
Got a DRM certificate from Google just now: the keybox is still valid
All good: streaming apps can play HD.
This ROM has no Widevine. Custom ROMs and GSIs need the vendor DRM files (Widevine HAL, liboemcrypto); only the ROM can fix it.
The Widevine service is not running, so apps fall back to L3. Reboot; if it stays down, the ROM or a module broke the DRM service.

No DRM certificate could be had. Check the network first; if it works, either the certificates on the device broke (getting them again below fixes that) or the keybox was revoked (only the maker can fix that).

Below L1 with the bootloader unlocked: the TEE may refuse L1 while unlocked, or the maker wiped the keybox on unlock. Getting the certificates again is worth one try; if it stays L3, only relocking the bootloader (stock boot, root removed first) can bring L1 back, and only when the keybox survived.

Below L1 with the bootloader locked (as the attestation says; a module that fakes attestation can make an unlocked device read locked): the keybox is most likely gone or revoked. Getting the certificates again is worth one try; otherwise the maker has to provision the device again.
Below L1 for a reason that cannot be told from here. Getting the certificates again is worth one try.

Saves the current DRM files, clears them, restarts the DRM services and asks the Google provisioning server for new certificates, as streaming apps do. If the device ends up worse, the old files go back. Streaming apps may have to download their offline content again.
This device is already L1, so there is nothing to fix. Go on only to try it: the old files go back if it ends up worse.
